extracted.intended_audience: legally-registered fact-checking organizations and fact-checking units within media organisations applying for IFCN signatory status
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and compliance criteria for organisations seeking to become IFCN signatories, covering eligibility, non-partisanship, sourcing, funding transparency, methodology, corrections, and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to be a signatory
rubrics_metrics.description: IFCN signatory status may be granted to legally registered organizations set up for the purpose of fact-checking that regularly publish non-partisan reports on the factual accuracy of statements by public figures and prominent institutions and widely circulated claims in text, visual and other formats focused primarily on claims related to public interest issues. IFCN signatory status may not be granted to organizations whose editorial work is controlled by the state, a political party or politician. It may however be granted to organizations that receive funding from state or political sources to carry out public service journalism if the IFCN assessor determines there is clear and unambiguous separation of editorial control from state or political influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be a legally registered organisation primarily set up for fact-checking and regularly publish non-partisan fact checks. State- or party-controlled editorial organisations are ineligible; organisations receiving state/political funding may be eligible only if assessors determine clear editorial independence. Read all criteria before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed by independent assessors for compliance with 31 criteria. Their assessment is reviewed by the IFCN advisory board to ensure fairness and consistency across the network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect independent assessment against the listed criteria and a further advisory-board review for consistency; applicants should provide documentation to demonstrate compliance with each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle #1 — A commitment to Non-partisanship and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations fact-check claims using the same standard for every fact check. They do not concentrate their fact-checking on any one side. They follow the same process for every fact check and let the evidence dictate the conclusions. Signatories do not advocate or take policy positions on the issues they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching expectation that the organisation's work is impartial, evidence-driven, and avoids advocacy or political alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpartisanship — equal standards of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant fact-checks using the same high standards of evidence and judgment for equivalent claims regardless of who made the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on whether identical methodological standards are applied across claims from different actors; internal policies and examples of past fact-checks can demonstrate this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection balance — not unduly concentrated on one side
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant does not unduly concentrate its fact-checking on any one side, considers the reach and importance of claims it selects to check and publishes a short statement on its website to set out how it selects claims to check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation should be able to show selection criteria and a public statement explaining claim selection, and demonstrate balanced coverage relative to reach/importance of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of sources' relevant interests and relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant discloses in its fact checks relevant interests of the sources it quotes where the reader might reasonably conclude those interests could influence the accuracy of the evidence provided. It also discloses in its fact checks any commercial or other such relationships it has that a member of the public might reasonably conclude could influence the findings of the fact check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact checks must include disclosures about potential conflicts of interest of cited sources and of the organisation itself when relevant to readers' assessment of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational political independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is not as an organization affiliated with nor declares or shows support for any party, any politician or political candidate, nor does it advocate for or against any policy positions on any issues save for transparency and accuracy in public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation should not publicly align with parties/politicians or advocate policy positions (except pro-transparency/accuracy). Evidence may include public statements, governance documents, and past activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff non-advocacy policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant sets out its policy on non-partisanship for staff on its site. Save for the issues of accuracy and transparency, the applicant's staff do not get involved in advocacy or publicize their views on policy issues the organization might fact-check in such a way as might lead a reasonable member of the public to see the organization's work as biased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a staff policy governing external/personal advocacy and publicizing of views that could create perception of organisational bias; demonstrate implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle #2 — A commitment to Standards and Transparency of Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories want their readers to be able to verify findings themselves. Signatories provide all sources in enough detail that readers can replicate their work, except in cases where a source's personal security could be compromised. In such cases, signatories provide as much detail as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching standard demanding verifiability and preference for transparency about sources while protecting vulnerable sources when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and citation of all significant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant identifies the source of all significant evidence used in their fact checks, providing relevant links where the source is available online, in such a way that users can replicate their work if they wish. In cases where identifying the source would compromise the source's personal security, the applicant provides as much detail as compatible with the source's safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations/links for significant evidence; where disclosure risks safety, provide maximum safe detail and explain constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary sources where available
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant uses the best available primary, not secondary, sources of evidence wherever suitable primary sources are available. Where suitable primary sources are not available, the applicant explains the use of a secondary source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer primary documentation/data; when relying on secondary sources, explicitly justify and explain their selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration from multiple named sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant checks all key elements of claims against more than one named source of evidence save where the one source is the only source relevant on the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checks should corroborate key elements with multiple named sources when feasible; single-source situations must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of sources' interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant identifies in its fact checks the relevant interests of the sources it uses where the reader might reasonably conclude those interests could influence the accuracy of the evidence provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose motivations, affiliations, or incentives of cited sources that could reasonably affect their credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle #3 — A commitment to Transparency of Funding & Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory organizations are transparent about their funding sources. If they accept funding from other organizations, they ensure that funders have no influence over the conclusions the fact-checkers reach in their reports. Signatory organizations detail the professional background of all key figures in the organization and explain the organizational structure and legal status. Signatories clearly indicate a way for readers to communicate with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect public disclosure of significant funders, organizational/legal form, leadership biographies, editorial control arrangements, and contact channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure page for independent organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants that are independent organizations have a page on their website detailing each source of funding accounting for 5% or more of total revenue for its previous financial year. This page also sets out the legal form in which the organization is registered (e.g. as a non-profit, as a company, etc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a funding page listing funders contributing >=5% of revenue for the previous year and state legal registration form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership statement for fact-checking units
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants that are the fact-checking section or unit of a media house or other parent organization make a statement on ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part of a parent organisation, clearly state ownership and relationship to parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational structure and editorial control statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement on the applicant's website sets out the applicant's organizational structure and makes clear how and by whom editorial control is exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish organisational chart/description and explicit explanation of editorial decision-making and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional biographies of key editorial figures
rubrics_metrics.description: A page on the applicant's website details the professional biography of all those who, according to the organizational structure and play a significant part in its editorial output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide bios for anyone playing a significant editorial role so readers can assess expertise and potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible communication channels for readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant provides easy means on its website and/or via social media for users to communicate with the editorial team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer clear, easy-to-find contact methods (email, forms, social media) for readers to reach the editorial team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle #4 — A commitment to Standards and Transparency of Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories explain the methodology they use to select, research, write, edit, publish and correct their fact checks. They encourage readers to send claims to fact-check and are transparent on why and how they fact-check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations must publish and follow an explicit methodology covering selection, research, writing, editing, publishing and corrections; encourage public submissions with clear expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a methodology statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant publishes on its website a statement about the methodology it uses to select, research, write and publish its fact checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make methodology publicly available and detailed enough to explain editorial workflows and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria based on reach and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant selects claims to check based primarily on the reach and importance of the claims, and where possible explains the reason for choosing the claim to check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate claim selection prioritisation by reach/importance and provide explanations for choices when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present evidence both supporting and undermining claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant sets out in its fact checks relevant evidence that appears to support the claim as well as relevant evidence that appears to undermine it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact checks should show balanced presentation of evidence pro and con to allow readers to see the basis for conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply same standards when assessing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant in its fact checks assesses the merits of the evidence found using the same high standards applied to evidence on equivalent claims, regardless of who made the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency in evidentiary assessment is required across all subjects and claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort to contact claimants and rules when contact is not possible
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant seeks where possible to contact those who made the claim to seek supporting evidence, noting that (I) this is often not possible with online claims, (II) if the person who makes the claim fails to reply in a timely way this should not impede the fact check, (III) if a speaker adds caveats to the claim, the fact-checker should be free to continue with checking the original claim, (IV) fact-checkers may not wish to contact the person who made the claim for safety or other legitimate reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make reasonable efforts to contact claimants but proceed when contact is impractical or unsafe; document attempts and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage reader submissions with clear expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant encourages users to send in claims to check, while making it clear what readers can legitimately expect will be fact-checked and what isn't fact-checkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide channels for reader submissions and a public explanation of scope/limitations of what will be fact-checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle #5 — A commitment to an Open & Honest Corrections Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories publish their corrections policy and follow it scrupulously. They correct clearly and transparently in line with the corrections policy, seeking so far as possible to ensure that readers see the corrected version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations must have and follow a visible corrections policy and proactively ensure corrections reach users of the original content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and accessible corrections/complaints policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has a corrections or complaints policy that is easily visible and accessible on the organization's website or frequently referenced in broadcasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections policy should be easy to find and referenced where relevant; demonstrate prominence and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy defines scope and handling of mistakes and complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The policy sets out clear definitions of what it does and does not cover, how major mistakes, especially those requiring revised conclusions of a fact check, are handled, and the fact that some complaints may justify no response. This policy is adhered to scrupulously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections/complaints policy must define covered issues, escalation for major errors, and circumstances where no response is appropriate; show consistent adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make transparent corrections when credible evidence of error
rubrics_metrics.description: Where credible evidence is provided that the applicant has made a mistake worthy of correction, the applicant makes corrections openly and transparently, seeking as far as possible to ensure that users of the original see the correction and the corrected version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct mistakes openly and take steps (e.g., linking, notifications) to make corrected versions visible to users of the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform readers about IFCN Code complaint route
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant, if an existing signatory, should either on its corrections/complaints page or on the page where it declares itself an IFCN signatory informs users that if they believe the signatory is violating the IFCN Code, they may inform the IFCN, with a link to the IFCN site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatories must include guidance on how readers can report potential Code violations to the IFCN, with a link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent company corrections policy requirement for units
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant is the fact-checking unit of a media company, it is a requirement for signatory status that the parent media company has and adheres to an open and honest corrections policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-checking units must ensure their parent company maintains and follows an appropriate corrections policy; provide evidence of parent adherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFCN Badge usage and signatory list
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations that have obtained IFCN verification are encouraged to publish a badge on their homepage. However, the complete list of signatories is here. Any other organization that holds the IFCN badge and is not listed is NOT a signatory to the Code of Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of the IFCN badge is encouraged for verified organisations, but applicants and readers should check the official signatory list to confirm status; unauthorised badge use does not indicate signatory status.
